thig13.5:1.1: “I was a child, with clean clothes,
thig13.5:1.2: when I first heard the Dhamma.
thig13.5:1.4: was a break-through to the truth.
thig13.5:2.2:
at an enormous dissatisfaction
with all sensuality.
thig13.5:5.1: it wouldn’t be proper for me—
thig13.5:5.3:
having cast off gold & silver
to take them back.
thig13.5:6.2:
don’t buy awakening,
don’t buy peace.
thig13.5:8.1:
It’s to this extent that many, many men
—heedless,
thig13.5:9.4:
Many misfortunes are seen
for those head-over-heels in sensuality.
thig13.5:10.2:
Why do you, like enemies,
try to bind me to sensuality?
thig13.5:11.2: can’t put an end to effluents.
thig13.5:11.3:
Sensuality is an enemy,
a murderer,
thig13.5:12.1:
So, my relatives:
Why do you,
thig13.5:12.2:
like enemies,
try to bind me to sensuality?
thig13.5:12.4: with shaven head, wrapped in a patchwork cloak.
thig13.5:13.2: a robe made from cast-off cloth:
thig13.5:13.4: the requisites of one with no home.
thig13.5:14.1: The great seers have rejected sensuality,
thig13.5:14.3:
Released are they,
in the place of security.
thig13.5:14.4:
Arrived are they,
in unshaken ease.
thig13.5:15.1:
So may I not come into union
with sensuality,
thig13.5:15.2: in which no shelter is found.
thig13.5:15.4: painful, like a mass of flame.
thig13.5:17.2:
Sensuality:
a frightening attack,
like a snake’s head
thig13.5:18.2:
Because many people in the world
are stuck in the mud of sensuality,
unknowing,
thig13.5:18.3: they don’t realize the ending of birth & death.
thig13.5:19.2:
Many people follow the path
to bad destinations
thig13.5:20.3: It’s the bait of the world,
thig13.5:21.4:
It’s a net cast by Māra
for the defilement of living beings:
thig13.5:22.4: drying up the good side [of the mind].
thig13.5:23.1: I, having cast off much trouble like this
thig13.5:23.4: as I always delight in unbinding.
thig13.5:24.2: in hopes of the cool state,
thig13.5:24.3: I will stay heedful, finding delight
thig13.5:25.4:
over which great seers
have crossed.”
thig13.5:26.1: See this Subhā, the goldsmith’s daughter,
thig13.5:26.4: doing jhāna at the foot of a tree.
thig13.5:27.1: This is the eighth day of her going forth
thig13.5:27.2: confident, beautiful through the true Dhamma.
thig13.5:27.4:
she’s a three-knowledge woman
who’s left death behind;
thig13.5:29.1:
Sakka, lord of beings,
with his community of devas,
thig13.5:29.4:
pays homage to her:
Subhā the goldsmith’s daughter.
